errors.english: an infinite jewel that cures fever
errors.why: མཐའ་ཡས here is the proper name of the serpent king Ananta: the stock example is the fever-curing jewel of the nāga, not an 'infinite jewel'.

fix.find: an infinite jewel that cures fever
fix.replace: the jewel of the serpent king Ananta that cures fever

errors.english: then the engagement based on a mistaken understanding of purpose will cease; or, if not mistaken, it will still result in withdrawal
errors.why: The Tibetan says that when the notion 'it has no purpose' is understood to be reversed one engages, and if it is not reversed one turns away; the English has engagement ceasing in both cases.

errors.english: If it were certain that the purpose of the subject matter is expressed
errors.why: ཅི་སྟེ here introduces the alternative the author affirms ('rather, it is certain that it states the purpose of the subject'), supported by the Dharmottara quote, not a hypothetical whose conclusion merely repeats its premise.

note: The argument about purpose and subject matter is followed in outline, but the Ananta example is mistranslated as a description and the engage/withdraw clause and the closing conclusion are garbled.

errors.english: If it were the universal
errors.why: སྤྱི here is the thesis taken as a whole (property plus subject, cf. the next side's སྤྱིའི་དོན 'sound is impermanent'), not a universal (jāti).

note: A generally sound rendering of the critique of the Nyāya and Vaiśeṣika definitions of the reason; the one problem is that སྤྱི (the whole thesis) is rendered as 'universal'.

errors.english: The phrase "at another time" means at the actual time the act is to be performed, not at any other time.
errors.why: The gloss says the admonition is to be done at another time, not at that very time.

fix.find: means at the actual time the act is to be performed, not at any other time.
fix.replace: means that it is to be done at another time, not at that very time.

errors.english: If one is exhorted by those who agree with him or through non-Dharmic means, there is no downfall. If one is exhorted by those who disagree with him but through Dharmic means
errors.why: མཐུན་པ / མི་མཐུན་པ are the Vinaya categories of a united (samagra) and a disunited (vyagra) saṅgha, and each case pairs the assembly with its manner (united but not in accordance with Dharma; disunited but in accordance with Dharma), not 'those who agree/disagree with him' joined by 'or'.

fix.find: If one is exhorted by those who agree with him or through non-Dharmic means, there is no downfall. If one is exhorted by those who disagree with him but through Dharmic means
fix.replace: If one is exhorted by a united (samagra) community but not in accordance with the Dharma, there is no downfall. If one is exhorted by a disunited (vyagra) community, even in accordance with the Dharma

errors.english: the tenth (Sanghadisesa) formal meeting of the Order
errors.why: In a Mūlasarvāstivāda text the category is the Sanskrit saṅghāvaśeṣa; the Pali form and the Pali etymology 'formal meeting of the Order' do not fit.

fix.find: the tenth (Sanghadisesa) formal meeting of the Order

note: The word commentary is mostly followed, but there is a reversed gloss on 'at another time', Pali terminology, and the samagra/vyagra distinction that governs the no-offence cases is lost.

errors.english: the inherent nature of the elements (bhuta) the physical elements: earth, water, fire, and air has thereby been negated
errors.why: What is negated is that attachment and the like are properties of the elements (their being bhūta-dharmas), not 'the inherent nature of the elements'.

fix.find: the inherent nature of the elements (bhuta) the physical elements: earth, water, fire, and air has thereby been negated
fix.replace: their being properties of the elements (bhuta) the physical elements: earth, water, fire, and air has thereby also been negated

errors.english: because of the fault that form and so forth are perceived by different sense organs
errors.why: The absurd consequence is that form and the rest would be grasped by a single sense faculty.

fix.find: because of the fault that form and so forth are perceived by different sense organs
fix.replace: because of the fault that form and so forth would then be grasped by a single sense faculty

errors.english: only those consciousnesses would become the support
errors.why: The Tibetan says that just as many consciousnesses would be supported (dependent on them), not that 'only those consciousnesses' would be the support.

note: The refutation of materialism is broadly followed, but key steps are misread: what is negated, the single-faculty absurdity, and which side is supported and which supports.

errors.english: it is untenable for an impermanent thing to be the transcendence of suffering in an ultimate sense
errors.why: The syllogism says that the impermanent cannot pass into nirvāṇa (as in MMK 16.4), not that it cannot 'be' nirvāṇa.

note: A faithful and clear rendering of Avalokitavrata on MMK 16.5; one syllogism is slightly misphrased.

errors.english: When one sees the fire and its burning one line of text follows
errors.why: 'one line of text follows' is a stray artefact with no Tibetan behind it; the side ends with 'when one sees fire and the like, burning...'.

fix.find: When one sees the fire and its burning one line of text follows
fix.replace: When one sees fire and the like, [its] burning...

errors.english: The opponent argues: "From the familiarity of others,"
errors.why: གཞན་གྱི marks this as the opponent's statement 'from familiarity...'; it is not familiarity 'of others'.

errors.english: Others, thinking that the experienced object cannot be denied, show the sequence
errors.why: The root text (the author) shows the sequence, anticipating that others might think the experienced matter cannot be denied; 'others' are not the ones who show it.

note: The objection-and-refutation sequence on the pramāṇa/non-pramāṇa distinction is followed well, but a stray artefact closes the side and two speaker attributions slip.

errors.english: at that time it is the (Tathagata) the One Thus Gone; a Buddha
errors.why: The verse (BCA 9.31) says that then all beings are Tathāgatas; the 'all' is lost.

fix.find: at that time it is the (Tathagata) the One Thus Gone; a Buddha
fix.replace: at that time all are (Tathagata) Ones Thus Gone; Buddhas

errors.english: Otherwise, it would be like space. Since a non-entity depends upon an entity, how can it possess the ability to act?
errors.why: The whole side is root verse of the Bodhicaryāvatāra (ch. 9) in four-line stanzas, but it is rendered as running prose paragraphs; the fix shows the lineation for the first stanza.

fix.find: Otherwise, it would be like space. Since a non-entity depends upon an entity, how can it possess the ability to act?
fix.replace:
Otherwise, it would be like space.
Since a non-entity depends upon an entity,
how can it possess the ability to act?

errors.english: Though the (Bodhisattva) one striving for awakening for the sake of others has passed into (Nirvana) the state beyond suffering, they still accomplish all purposes.
errors.why: It is the Jina-pillar that accomplishes all aims even after the bodhisattva has passed into nirvāṇa (BCA 9.38), not the bodhisattva.

errors.english: through the power of the aspirations of those to be trained
errors.why: The verse (BCA 9.36, vineyapraṇidhānābhyām) names two causes, the disciples and the bodhisattva's vows; the English makes the vows the disciples' own.

note: The content of BCA 9.29–40 is mostly tracked, but the verse is flattened into prose, 'all are Tathāgatas' is lost, and the agent of the Garuḍa-pillar simile is misassigned.

errors.english: the "seeker" who seeks refers to the causal mental states of the past, while the "having sought" refers to the resultant mental states of the future
errors.why: བྱེད་པ་པོ / ལས here are the grammatical agent (kartṛ) and object (karman) of seeking (earlier and later moments of mind), not 'causal' and 'resultant' states.

errors.english: While intention arises from generation
errors.why: The Tibetan says that although intention does not deviate from (is inseparable from) generation, 'generation' is still mentioned to specify it; it does not say that intention arises from generation.

note: A good rendering of the bodhicitta definition and the AA 1.4 verse; there are minor slips in the agent/object analysis.

errors.english: Answering the statement made by the opponent, the author says:
errors.why: This introduces the opponent's anticipated rejoinder (that 'cook' lacks a universal yet recurrent cognitions have another cause), which the author then refutes with 'the primary factor' and so forth; the English gives it to the author.

fix.find: Answering the statement made by the opponent, the author says:
fix.replace: Anticipating a reply to what was said, the opponent says:

errors.english: if one attempts to prove that there is some other cause once the universal has been set aside
errors.why: སྤྱི here means 'in general' (sāmānyena), in contrast with ཁྱད་པར་སྒྲུབ་ན 'if one proves a specific one' in the next sentence; it is not 'setting aside the universal'.

fix.find: if one attempts to prove that there is some other cause once the universal has been set aside
fix.replace: if one attempts to prove in general that there is some other cause

note: The apoha refutation is followed in substance, but the opening opponent's argument is given to the author and the general/specific dilemma is misread.

errors.english: (tarka) sophistry or fallacious argument
errors.why: ལྟག་ཆོད is jāti, the futile rejoinder, not tarka.

errors.english: of the nature of perceiving a pervading contradiction
errors.why: This is the technical reason type 'perception of what is pervaded by a contradictory' (viruddhavyāptopalabdhi), not the perception of a pervading contradiction.

errors.english: Although these two are not mistaken
errors.why: The Tibetan says 'although these are not deviated by those two', so the two are what would cause the deviation, not the items that are not mistaken.

note: The terse pratīka commentary is handled competently; there are a few logic-term errors (jāti, viruddhavyāptopalabdhi).
